questions.question: In MCP 2026-07-28, who decides when a particular prompt is invoked?
options: The user selects it explicitly, since prompts are designed to be user controlled
The model selects it automatically whenever the conversation needs more context
The server schedules it automatically on a fixed recurring time interval
The host renders it without asking the user or the model at all
questions.explanation: Prompts are user-controlled: a server authors their content, but the user is the one who explicitly selects when a prompt runs, often through a menu or slash command.

questions.question: A client calls prompts/get for a prompt with one required argument and supplies no arguments at all. What does a conformant server return?
options: A JSON-RPC error with code -32601 because the prompt itself is missing
A JSON-RPC error with code -32602 because a required argument is missing
An input_required result that asks the model to supply the value
A normal result whose messages array is simply left completely empty
questions.explanation: Missing a required prompt argument is a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 Invalid params; -32601 is reserved for a method the server does not implement at all.

questions.question: A completion/complete request matches 137 possible values for one argument. How many does the result's values array contain, and what else must it report?
options: Zero values, because completion refuses requests above 100 possible matches
All 137 values plus a total field and hasMore set to false
At most 100 values, with hasMore true since more matches exist
Exactly 10 values by default, with pagination handled by a cursor
questions.explanation: A completion result never carries more than 100 ranked values; when more matches exist than that cap, the result also sets hasMore to true so the client knows the list was cut short.

questions.question: A client is completing a prompt's second argument and has already resolved the first one. How should it help the server narrow the suggestions?
options: Repeat the first argument inside the value field of the one being completed
Send a separate tools/call first so the server remembers the earlier answer
Open a subscriptions/listen stream and publish the earlier answer onto it
Carry the earlier answer in context.arguments on the completion request
questions.explanation: completion/complete accepts a context.arguments map of already-resolved argument names to values, which lets the server narrow suggestions for the argument currently being typed.

questions.question: A prompt message needs to point at a large reference file without inlining its bytes into the message. Which content type fits that job?
options: A resource_link block with the file's uri, a name, and its mime type
An audio block, since resource references are only valid for sound content
A text block that copies the entire file inline as one long block of text
An image block, since resource references are only valid for picture content
questions.explanation: A resource_link content block lets a prompt message point at a resource by uri, name, and mime type without embedding the resource's full contents in the message.

questions.question: A client sends prompts/list with a cursor value the server never issued. What should a conformant server do with that request?
options: Silently ignore the bad cursor and return the very first page again
Reject the request with a JSON-RPC error, code -32602 invalid params
Treat the cursor as valid and return an empty prompts array only
Start an entirely new connection and replay the whole prompt catalog
questions.explanation: Cursors are opaque tokens the server itself issues; a cursor the server does not recognize is an invalid parameter and must be rejected with error code -32602.
